item.description: Tiger Woods was on hand with Rob McNamara, Executive Vice President of TGR, Tiger Woods Ventures, for son Charlie Woods' signing day Ceremony at Benjamin High School on Nov. 6, 2026. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Tiger Woods made the correct call by turning down a reported $750 million offer to join LIV Golf, a decision that now looks prescient as the league officially folds. Since its 2022 launch, the breakaway circuit, which Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund supports, has spent over $5 billion to attract elite players from the PGA Tour. That massive financial push failed to secure a sustainable future, leaving the organization in bankruptcy court with no path forward. Woods avoided the fallout entirely, while former stars like Jon Rahm now face an uncertain professional landscape without the league they once joined. The collapse of the LIV Golf project was confirmed during a bankruptcy hearing in New Jersey on Thursday. Gibson Dunn’s Attorney Matthew Williams informed the court that the league failed to secure an agreement capable of enabling financially sustainable restructuring. Williams stated, “The debtors are not currently proceeding with the LIV 2.0 plan,” marking the end of any hopes for a scaled-down revival, according to Yahoo Sports . After BC Partners Credit withdrew its proposed $300 million investment, which was meant to supplant the Saudi PIF as the main financier, the announcement was made. Without that capital, the league is shifting its focus. Williams explained, “Instead, the debtors are toggling to a value-maximizing wind-down in their business.” Tiger Woods understood the risks before the league even began its aggressive recruitment. In a Friday column, The Athletic’s Ian O’Connor described Woods’ perspective on the offer, observing that the golfer no longer needed to struggle for earnings. Woods questioned whether the new league offered anything beyond cash for the world’s best players. O’Connor wrote, “There’s that word again, dirt,” capturing Woods’ hesitation about the environment the league promised, according to Yahoo Sports . The sentiment was that LIV lacked the competitive spirit that drives golfers to chase perfection. O’Connor noted, “At its highest decibels, LIV offered none of that,” referring to the legacy and immortality that Jack Nicklaus and Sam Snead chased throughout their careers. This missing element is why Woods turned down the $750 million and why Nicklaus declined over $100 million to run the show. item.title: De Zerbi focuses on Spurs' failings - but should Bogle have seen red?
item.description: It was somewhat surprising to see Roberto de Zerbi take a more peaceful approach when he faced the media at Elland Road after Tottenham's 1-0 defeat by Leeds United on Saturday afternoon. The Spurs manager had been expected to come out swinging in the direction of the officials after his side's first Premier League loss since September, with much of the focus falling on referee John Brooks' decision not to send Jayden Bogle off for a late challenge on Mathys Tel during the first half. It was a decision that no doubt impacted the game - and perhaps Tottenham's chances of earning a fourth consecutive Premier League victory for the first time since October 2023. When Bogle caught Tel with his studs, the game was still goalless and Tottenham were arguably the team on top at Elland Road. But that quickly changed. Following a lengthy video assistant referee (VAR) check that lasted more than four minutes, no further action was taken against the Leeds defender and the game resumed. That was not the case for Frenchman Tel, who was unable to continue after sustaining a bruising injury to his left foot. Former Premier League assistant referee Darren McCann said Bogle was "fortunate" not to be dismissed. "Bogle's challenge meets the criteria for serious foul play as he endangers the safety of an opponent," McCann told BBC Sport. "He can consider himself lucky to still be on the pitch." By the time play resumed, there was less than nine minutes of the first half remaining and Tottenham's momentum - and composure - were fading quickly. De Zerbi's side never appeared to recover from the incident and, after the break, were outrun, outworked and outplayed by the home side. Nevertheless, De Zerbi - perhaps buoyed by his side's recent rise up the table - refused to pinpoint Spurs' failings on the referee's decision. "We deserved to lose the game in the second half and didn't play like we can," he told TNT Sports. "It's a journey for us because we can learn from this game. "I am sorry for the performance in the second half - we didn't play like a top team. We didn't have the right character and physicality in the second half." item.title: Barnesville ousts Martins Ferry to set up Division V regional clash with Girard
item.description: BARNESVILLE −Barnesville senior Trey Toliver spent the regular season rewriting the Shamrock record books. On Friday, Nov. 6, he added another historic chapter – and gave Martins Ferry a full-strength reminder of why he's one of the state's premier running backs. Entering the OHSAA Division V, Region 17 postseason as Barnesville's all-time leading rusher with 5,458 yards and 95 career touchdowns, Toliver put on a clinic, racking up 276 yards and four touchdowns on 28 carries to lead the second-seeded Shamrocks to a 35-18 victory over Purple Riders at Shamrock Stadium. The victory kept Barnesville's perfect season intact at 11-0 and punched their ticket into the regional semifinals. More than an impressive opening act in the OHSSA football postseason, Friday's performance from the dynamic Toliver served as a stark redo. Back on Oct. 10 at Martins Ferry, the Purple Riders gave Barnesville all they could handle in a tight 25-21 decision, holding Toliver to a rare off night of 160 yards on 26 carries. Round 2 between the Buckeye 8 Conference foes was a completely different story. Martins Ferry had contained Toliver once, but in the high-stakes atmosphere of the OHSAA postseason, the Purple Riders got the full, unrelenting dose of the senior's dynamic abilities on the gridiron. Barnesville head coach Blake Allen praised his squad's complete game effort up front and the dominant ground attack that took over in the second half. "Offensively our line played outstanding and really controlled the line of scrimmage," Allen said. "And Trey had another unbelievable performance. He was running hard, and taking advantage of the work our O-line was getting done. Just an all-around great effort on both sides of the ball tonight." "We worked on cleaning up some of our mistakes on defense over the bye week," Allen added. "And for the most part, we held a very explosive team in check tonight. So really proud of the way our kids performed tonight." Carpenter sets the early tone Martins Ferry struck first with Walkquem Cox scoring on a short 1-yard plunge for a 6-0 Purple Riders lead with just 40.8 seconds left in the first quarter. Barnesville senior QB Colt Carpenter provided the answer to open the Shamrocks scoring, capping a second quarter scoring drive with a 1-yard dive into the end zone, giving Barnesville a 7-6 lead with 5:33 remaining in the frame. Carpenter also connected on his lone pass attempt of the night, hitting sophomore Knoxx Mankin with a 7-yard completion, and finished with 21 yards rushing on six attempts with his touchdown. Toliver takes over Once Carpenter put the Shamrocks on top, Toliver took over the heavy lifting. The senior standout answered a second quarter Martins Ferry score with a 21-yard touchdown run to give Barnesville a 14-12 edge heading into the locker room at halftime. item.title: Luka Doncic’s 50-burger vs. Blazers puts Lakers star in history books next to Wilt Chamberlain
item.description: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images. Luka Doncic’s 50-burger vs. Blazers puts Lakers star in history books next to Wilt Chamberlain appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Luka Doncic scored a season-high 53 points in the Los Angeles Lakers ’ 124-118 win over the Portland Trail Blazers Friday night, joining Wilt Chamberlain as the only players in NBA history to average at least 40 points through their first nine appearances of a season. Doncic’s 40.1-point average trails only Chamberlain’s starts in 1962-63 and 1961-62, when he averaged 52.4 and 50.6 points, respectively. The comparison covers individual appearances, rather than all 10 games the Lakers have played. ClutchPoints highlighted the milestone Saturday on X, formerly Twitter, sharing a broadcast graphic that illustrated Doncic’s place alongside Chamberlain. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The most PPG through the first 9 games by any player in NBA history 🔥 (1962-63) Wilt Chamberlain — 52.4 (1961-62) Wilt Chamberlain — 50.6 (2026-27) Luka Doncic — 40.1 pic.twitter.com/mNIAdoucAy — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 7, 2026 Doncic, 27, shot 17 of 33 from the field, including 5 of 15 from 3-point range, and made 14 of 18 free throws at Crypto.com Arena. He also contributed five rebounds and five assists. The outing marked his 11th career 50-point game, tying Allen Iverson for 10th in NBA history. Four of those performances have come with the Lakers. Doncic has dropped at least 40 points in six of his last seven games, including each of his last four. He joins Elgin Baylor , Kobe Bryant and George Mikan as the only Lakers with four consecutive 40-point regular-season games. Bryant last accomplished the feat in 2012. Friday’s scoring burst helped Los Angeles erase a 16-point deficit against a Trail Blazers team that entered atop the Western Conference standings. Doncic scored 20 points in the third quarter, outscoring the Blazers’ entire team by five during the period. The Slovenian superstar capped his 53-point performance with a jumper in the lane with 27 seconds left, sealing the Lakers’ comeback as they improved to 8-2 with their fourth straight win. item.title: Burkardt saves the day for Frankfurt in Paderborn as penalty king Atubolu delivers in different way
item.description: Burkardt saves the day for Frankfurt in Paderborn as penalty king Atubolu delivers in different way Adi Hütter surprisingly left Germany international Younes Ebnoutalib on the bench, but fellow striker Jonathan Burkardt gave them an early lead at the midpoint of a lively first-half. Ritsu Doan and Lillian Brassier had the game's first chances inside the first ten minutes. Noah Atubolu's first save arrived minutes later as he parried away Gabriel Vidovic's curling effort. Against the run of play, the visitors took the lead as Fares Chaïbi punished Paderborn's disorganized defense with a brilliant assist for Burkardt. Stefano Marino hit the crossbar five minutes later before Chaïbi nearly added a goal to his assist. The hosts got a deserved equalizer just before the half-time break as the unmarked Raphael Obermair nutmegged Atubolu with a quickfire finish. After his assist to Obermair's goal, Ruben Müller nearly scored early after the restart before another decent chance for US midfielder Santiago Castaneda. Chaïbi also had a chance for his second direct goal involvement inside the lively ten minutes right after the half-time break. With 25 minutes left to play, both coaches already made seven substitutions in total. 16-year-old midfielder Niko Ilicevic entered the scene for his second Bundesliga appearance, but Paderborn took the lead for the first time after he was dispossessed in the danger zone. Brassier had a difficult game, and he committed a foul on substitute Marvin Pieringer inside the box. Atubolu, who saved all the previous six penalty-kicks he has faced at Freiburg and Frankfurt, dived the right way, but he wasn't able to deny Pieringer his first Paderborn goal. Frankfurt's hopes of getting back to the game faced a huge blow a couple of minutes later as Elias Baum saw his second yellow card. Ralf Kettemann subbed off half-time substitute Deniz Zeitler in fear of a similar outcome, but the hosts failed to hold on to their slender lead. Atubolu's penalty-kick record came to an end, but he guided Chaïbi's corner-kick to Burkardt's direction as the striker leveled the score with an unorthodox finish in the last action of the game. Paderborn tied a club-record four Bundesliga games unbeaten run, but they have only beaten HSV in this run. Frankfurt will be in eight place as the Bundesliga will now take a second international break.

item.title: FIFA reduce ban for Argentina & Roma defender Nahuel Molina following 2026 World Cup final brawl
item.description: England v Argentina: Semi Final - FIFA World Cup 2026 - Getty Images Sport Argentina and Roma defender Nahuel Molina has received a significant boost after FIFA agreed to reduce his lengthy international suspension. The ban was originally issued following the chaotic scenes that marred the conclusion of the 2026 World Cup final earlier this summer, which Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain in extra time. Appeal success for Molina The Argentine Football Association (AFA) has successfully lobbied for a reduction in the disciplinary sanctions handed out to Molina. The Roma full-back was initially hit with a seven-match suspension and a $77,000 fine for his part in the post-match fracas that followed the tournament's showpiece event in East Rutherford. Following a formal review of the incident, FIFA's appeals committee decided to lower the defender's punishment to a four-game ban, while also reducing his fine to $60,000. Road to redemption Molina has already made significant progress in serving his time away from the pitch. The right-back sat out Argentina's recent trio of friendly victories against Bolivia, Burkina Faso, and Benin in October. With three games already accounted for, he now has only one match remaining on his revised four-game suspension. Despite the reduction, the defender was left out of Lionel Scaloni's latest Argentina squad, announced earlier this week ahead of November's international friendlies against Uruguay and Costa Rica. Serie A presence remains While Molina's suspension was reduced, Leandro Paredes saw his 10-match ban and $90,000 fine upheld for his role in the World Cup final brawl. Although both players remain sidelined, Scaloni's squad continues to lean heavily on Italian top-flight talent, with seven Serie A representatives included in the latest Argentina roster as the team moves past the summer's drama. Among the call-ups are Molina's Roma colleagues Leonardo Balerdi, Matias Soule, and Santiago Castro, ensuring the Giallorossi remain well-represented. They are joined by Como duo Nico Paz and Maxi Perrone, Parma's Mariano Troilo, and Fiorentina's Franco Mastantuono to complete the seven-man Serie A contingent. Molina's club form and Roma's title push On the club front, Molina has made 11 appearances for Roma across all competitions this season, scoring once in the Champions League and providing two assists in Serie A. His performances have helped the Giallorossi build a strong campaign, with Roma currently sitting third in the Serie A table on 24 points - just four points adrift of leaders Lazio.

item.description: CHAMPAIGN, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 06: Anthony Colandrea #10 of the Nebraska Cornhuskers dives for a first down as he is tackled by Tanner Heckel #16 of the Illinois Fighting Illini during the first half at Gies Memorial Stadium on November 06, 2026 in Champaign, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is how the first half went for the Nebraska offense. 1st Offensive Drive – Two Penalties. Punt. 2nd Offensive Drive – Two Penalties. Missed Field Goal. 3rd Offensive Drive – Zero penalties. Touchdown . 4th Offensive Drive – One Penalty. Punt. 5th Offensive Drive – One Penalty. Missed Field Goal. Here is how the second half went for the Nebraska offense. 6th Offensive Drive – Zero penalties. Failed on 4th-and-1 from Illinois 25 yard line because of zero confidence in a kicker. 7th Offensive Drive – Zero Penalties. Touchdown . 8th Offensive Drive – Two Penalties. Failed on 4th-and-3 from Illinois 34 yard line. One of the penalties was the personal foul blindside block that was completely unnecessary. Instead of a 2nd-and-8, the result was 1st-and-25. 9th Offensive Drive – Zero Penalties. End of Game. Penalties have been one of the major stories of this season. First, and the most obvious have been bizarre illegal blind side block penalties at the worst times throughout the season. Second, have been procedural penalties. Both bizarre and infuriating in different ways. The illegal blind side block, I would understand, if it was once earlier in this season. You could say that it was somebody trying to make a play to help the team. However, after the first one or two, especially after it negated a huge gain and possibly cost the team a win then I would simply not do it again. The procedural penalties on the other hand are a different animal. A perfect example would be on the first possession against Illinois. Anthony Colandrea completed a 17-yard pass to Jamal Rule which set Nebraska up at the Illinois 37 for a first down. Except for that Illegal Motion penalty by Jacory Barney. So instead of 1st-and-10 from the Illinois 37, it is now 3rd-and-7 from the Nebraska 41 yard line. Nebraska ends up having to punt. Archie Wilson punts it to Illinois’ 20 yard line. Not bad. Oh wait. Another procedural penalty. This time is was Illegal Formation. Nebraska punts again and instead of the 20-yard line, Illinois now starts from their own 29. There are teams in college football that can survive drive-crippling penalties. Nebraska is not one of those teams. Offensively it just appears that nothing comes easy for the offense. That is usually because they find themselves behind the sticks at the worst possible times. Staying “on schedule” is so important for Dana Holgorsen and the offense that these “simple” procedural penalties are crippling. item.title: Why Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty against Hull despite Kai Havertz being offside
item.description: Arsenal FC v Hull City - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Arsenal were denied a penalty against Hull City on Saturday after VAR ruled Kai Havertz offside before he was hauled down by Nobel Mendy. Home fans briefly celebrated when referee Farai Hallam first announced the foul, but Hull were instead awarded a free kick, leaving Mikel Arteta fuming on the touchline during a tense first half at the Emirates Stadium. Arsenal denied penalty after lengthy VAR review against Hull Arsenal were on top for much of the first half and thought they had a chance to score from 12 yards when Havertz went down in the box under a challenge from Mendy. Play continued, but the incident was assessed by VAR for a number of minutes before Hallam was advised to consult the pitchside monitor. The VAR told the referee that Mendy had clearly held the striker's shirt, but that Havertz was offside at the time, so the foul could not be given. Emirates celebrations turn to anger as Arteta confronts officials When Hallam announced the decision, he spoke of the foul by the Hull centre-back first, and the home faithful cheered the penalty they thought was coming. Their delight turned to disappointment in the blink of an eye when he explained that Hull would instead take a free kick for offside. A Premier League statement read: "VAR recommended an on-field review for a potential penalty to Arsenal for a challenge by Mendy on Havertz - but determined that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up." The call sparked outrage among the Arsenal players and on the bench, with Arteta having stern words with the fourth official before the teams went in goalless at the break. Why VAR got the Havertz offside call wrong It soon emerged that the rules were on Arsenal's side. BBC Sport's football issues correspondent Dale Johnson said: "That is a very controversial VAR intervention at the Emirates. A player who is in an offside position only becomes active when they commit an offside offence. Kai Havertz must be 'attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball' - otherwise the shirt pull by Nobel Mendy takes precedence. The foul comes before any offside offence. "Havertz did not commit an offside offence, and this should have been a spot-kick to Arsenal regardless of the offside. We saw this a couple of seasons ago between Newcastle and Bournemouth. Fabian Schar was just offside but pulled back as he moved to run onto a free-kick delivery. A penalty was awarded after a VAR review." What next for Arsenal in the second half against Hull? The decision leaves the defending champions with a real sense of injustice at half-time. Arteta's side must now turn that frustration into a breakthrough after the restart, and if the goal does not come, the questions for the officials will only grow louder.

item.title: Keegan tribute display sees thousands of visitors
item.description: A display was made using tributes to footballer Kevin Keegan [Newcastle United Football Club] An exhibition featuring hundreds of shirts left outside Newcastle's stadium in tribute to Kevin Keegan has seen thousands of visitors. Flowers, cards, shirts and scarves were placed at St James' Park by fan s of the footballing legend in the days following his death on 20 July at the age of 75 . A free event at the Baltic Centre for Contemporary Art last weekend, which featured a 57ft (17.5m) banner designed by fan group Wor Flags and a commemorative film celebrating Keegan, saw 3,805 people visit. Designer Dan Lycett said it was his "most stressful" display so far because of what Keegan meant to him, saying: "He was my hero so I had to get it right." Although not from Newcastle, Keegan was loved and admired by Geordies thanks to the influential stints he had as both a player and manager at the city's football club in the 1980s and '90s. Gifted, charismatic and passionate amid highs and lows - Keegan obituary Keegan death unites Liverpool and Hamburg - mayor He was posthumously awarded the Freedom of Newcastle earlier this week . Thousands of people visited the temporary exhibition last weekend [Newcastle United Football Club] "It was a very emotional piece," Lycett said. "Just the word legend, but within that legend was shirts from many, many different teams that he touched." As a player, Keegan helped secure promotion back to the First Division and as a manager, led the club up to the Premier League where his famous Entertainers team came close to winning the title. Keegan went on to manage Fulham, Manchester City and England, before returning to Tyneside for a second spell in charge in 2008. Newcastle United could not yet confirm plans for what would happen with the display. Follow BBC Newcastle on X , Facebook , Nextdoor and Instagram , and listen to Radio Newcastle on BBC Sounds . item.title: Kimmich inspires Bayern win at Mainz but Dortmund keep pace
item.description: Bayern Munich's Joshua Kimmich scores his side's first goal during the German Bundesliga soccer match between 1. FSV Mainz 05 and FC Bayern Munichat Mewa Arena. (is associated with: «Kimmich inspires Bayern win at Mainz but Dortmund keep pace») Torsten Silz/dpa Joshua Kimmich's first Bundesliga goal of the season helped injury-hit Bayern Munich win 2-1 at Mainz on Saturday and stay top of the table on goal difference. Borussia Dortmund remain level on points with the champions after overcoming promoted Elversberg 2-1 at home thanks to Felix Nmecha's second-half double. The Germany midfielder first rifled home from outside the box after being set up by Fabio Silva, who again impressed with striker Serhou Guirassy out injured. Nmecha added the clincher with an equally memorable strike before Noel Futkeu's goal for Elversberg prompted a nervous finale in Dortmund. Kimmich's finish from 20 metres was similarly emphatic for Bayern and Harry Kane also assisted Lennart Karl for 2-0 after the break. The champions, already missing Luis Diaz, Jamal Musiala, Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry, prevailed in Mainz despite suffering another big-name injury. Manuel Neuer, who became the oldest Bayern player in the Bundesliga aged 40 years and 225 days old, was substituted with a recurring foot problem just after flapping at a cross. He was relieved to see a Mainz equalizer ruled out by VAR for a tight offside as he hobbled off. Mainz, who lost for the fourth game in a row in all competitions, have not won at home in the Bundesliga since March and substitute Phillip Tietz's goal came too late. A medical emergency in the away end meant fans refrained from noise for much of the first half, just like at Paderborn's 2-2 home draw with Eintracht Frankfurt. The 10-man Eagles levelled in stoppage time after goalkeeper Noah Atubolu went up the other end and flicked on for Jonathan Burkardt to score a classy second. RB Leipzig are third after nine games having come from behind to hammer Augsburg 5-2. The 12th-placed visitors scored in the first minute through Anton Kade, but their early season form has deserted them. Ezechiel Banzuzi, Christopher Nkunku and dropped Germany left back David Raum netted before half-time, with Rômulo and Christoph Baumgartner scoring after the hour and Uchenna Ogundu adding a consolation. On Friday, bottom side Borussia Mönchengladbach lost 3-1 at Hamburg. VfB Stuttgart host in-form Werder Bremen in Saturday's late game and there are three matches on Sunday, including Cologne against derby rivals Bayer Leverkusen and fourth-placed Freiburg welcoming Union Berlin. item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 28: Jacob Misiorowski #32 of the Milwaukee Brewers reacts during the fifth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game five of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field on October 28, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s not Tarik Skubal and Adrian Morejon, but when you make two huge moves and both meet the approval of even Trainman, you’ve done something right. You would have to be quite the fanatical follower, or at least a fan of the Red Sox or Brewers, to even have been familiar with two names that will lead the A’s gently into that good desert. Taylor Smith is such a household name, if you search “Taylor Smith” Google’s first result is a question: “Did you mean Taylor Swift?” At this point you just say “yes,” click on the first few links and forget that you were thinking about baseball. Cam Castro may be famous to his family and friends but few outside of Wisconsin could have told you much about his work. Out of all the Castros throughout history his fame ranking is relatively low, as there are no known political regimes nor neighborhood districts in his name. Yet Smith and Castro come with just the credentials the A’s need right now as they try to rebuild their analytic, development, and trading/acquisition models to work more like, say, the Brewers and Rays. Those 2 teams have a couple things in common: they just met in the World Series and Castro/Smith previously spent the most seasons with their organization. As GM, Castro will have a big hand in who the A’s acquire, who they keep and who they let go, but perhaps his most essential expertise comes in his record of helping to bring out the best in pitchers yet to tap into their potential. The hope would be that instead of spinning valuable players like Shea Langeliers and Tyler Soderstrom into worthy pitching talent, perhaps those gems can be culled from Luis Morales and Jack Perkins, who certainly have the physical tools. Meanwhile, as PBO Smith comes with experience watching both sides of the payroll scale, starting with the frugal-but-shrewd Rays and continuing with the big market Red Sox. He will draw more from his understanding of how the Rays operate, but if his first big move (sorry Nate Eaton) was to select Castro to put a spotlight on the pitching side, Smith appears to be “1 for 1” and demonstrating a clear understanding not just of the need for the A’s to emphasize pitching but also to develop it beyond just bringing”adding good pitchers to the roster”. item.title: Jersey Bulls' unbeaten run ends in dramatic late loss
item.description: Jersey Bulls had not lost an Isthmian League game in 2026 [BBC] Jersey Bulls' 34-match Isthmian League unbeaten run came to an end as they lost 3-2 at Hartley Wintney. The defeat was the Isthmian League South Central leaders' first since 30 December 2025, having been undefeated in 33 league games and drawing 0-0 in the play-off semi-final before losing on penalties. The island side thought they had sealed a point when Toby Ritzema made it 2-2 in the 86th minute. But the hosts scored in the fourth minute of stoppage time to earn a dramatic win. Having won manager of the month Jersey boss Elliot Powell saw his side go behind in the 10th-minute when Bulls' Harry Curtis headed down a corner and Jonny Efedje blasted in from close range. Manager of month Powell targets Jersey Bulls title Jersey Bulls' midfielder Mohamed wins historic call-up Sammy Henia-Kamau had a half-chance for the Bulls midway through the first half before winning a penalty 10 minutes later when his shot was blocked by a Hartley hand and skipper James Queree converted from the spot. Jersey could have gone ahead a minute later when top scorer Lorne Bickley saw a header well saved by home goalkeeper. But they fell behind again just before the half-time whistle when Efedje's effort from a cross crept in over the line having come off the post. Fraser Barlow blasted an effort just over the home bar 20 minutes into the second half while Henia-Kamau had an effort saved soon after. Having put the hosts under pressure it looked as the island side had salvaged their unbeaten run when Henia-Kamau had a shot saved and Ritzema was first to react.
